name: Google Sheets
hint: A web OAuth client in your Google Cloud project with the Google Sheets API enabled, and one account’s refresh token for this scope under https://www.googleapis.com/auth/: spreadsheets, for example from the OAuth 2.0 Playground; an External app left in Testing gets tokens that end after 7 days.

endpoints.name: get_spreadsheet
endpoints.description: Returns a spreadsheet’s title, locale and time zone, and each sheet’s properties, formatting and protected ranges, with no cell data unless fields asks for it. Without fields the answer can be large: fields=sheets.properties(sheetId,title) lists the sheets. ranges takes one range in A1 notation, for example Sheet1!A1:D20, and keeps only the parts of the spreadsheet that intersect it. spreadsheetId is in the spreadsheet’s address: docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/SPREADSHEET_ID/edit.

notes.fields: Selector specifying which fields to include in a partial response.
notes.ranges: The ranges to retrieve from the spreadsheet.

endpoints.name: get_values
endpoints.description: Returns the values of a range in A1 notation, for example Sheet1!A1:D20 or 'Q3 Sales'!A:C (quote a sheet name with spaces); empty trailing rows and columns are left out. valueRenderOption is FORMATTED_VALUE (the default), UNFORMATTED_VALUE or FORMULA, and dateTimeRenderOption is SERIAL_NUMBER (the default) or FORMATTED_STRING.

notes.spreadsheetId: The ID of the spreadsheet to retrieve data from.
notes.range: The [A1 notation or R1C1 notation](https://developers.google.com/workspace/sheets/api/guides/concepts#cell) of the range to retrieve values from.
notes.majorDimension: The major dimension that results should use. For example, if the spreadsheet data in Sheet1 is: `A1=1,B1=2,A2=3,B2=4`, then requesting `range=Sheet1!A1:B2?majorDimension=ROWS` returns `[[1,2],[3,4]]`, whereas requesting `range=Sheet1!A1:B2?majorDimension=COLUMNS` returns `[[1,3],[2,4]]`.
notes.valueRenderOption: How values should be represented in the output. The default render option is FORMATTED_VALUE.
notes.dateTimeRenderOption: How dates, times, and durations should be represented in the output. This is ignored if value_render_option is FORMATTED_VALUE. The default dateTime render option is SERIAL_NUMBER.

endpoints.name: create_spreadsheet
endpoints.description: Creates a spreadsheet in the root folder of the account’s Google Drive and returns it, with its spreadsheetId and spreadsheetUrl. Body: {"properties": {"title": "Budget 2027"}}.

endpoints.name: update_values
endpoints.description: Writes values into a range in A1 notation, for example Sheet1!A1:D20. valueInputOption is required: USER_ENTERED reads each value as if typed into Sheets (formulas, dates, numbers), RAW stores it as it is. Body: {"values": [["A1", "B1"], ["A2", "B2"]]}.

notes.spreadsheetId: The ID of the spreadsheet to update.
notes.range: The [A1 notation](https://developers.google.com/workspace/sheets/api/guides/concepts#cell) of the values to update.
notes.valueInputOption: How the input data should be interpreted.

endpoints.name: append_values
endpoints.description: Appends rows after the table of data found in a range in A1 notation; Sheet1 searches the whole sheet. valueInputOption is required (USER_ENTERED or RAW); by default the rows overwrite what follows the table, and insertDataOption=INSERT_ROWS inserts new rows instead. Body: {"values": [["Ada", "2027-01-31", 42]]}.

notes.spreadsheetId: The ID of the spreadsheet to update.
notes.range: The [A1 notation](https://developers.google.com/workspace/sheets/api/guides/concepts#cell) of a range to search for a logical table of data. Values are appended after the last row of the table.
notes.valueInputOption: How the input data should be interpreted.
notes.insertDataOption: How the input data should be inserted.
